project.name: siard-suite
project.description: SIARD Suite is a toolset for archiving relational databases in the SIARD 2.2 (Software-Independent Archival of Relational Databases) format, ensuring long-term preservation independent of the original DBMS. Includes a JavaFX desktop GUI, command-line tools, a core SIARD read/write API, and database-specific JDBC wrappers.

nodes.summary: Coordinates batched loading: keeps the complete list and the filtered observable list in sync, deduplicates already-loaded batches, and reports loading progress.

nodes.name: applyFilter

nodes.name: clearFilter
nodes.summary: Drops the current filter and restores the observable list to all loaded items.

nodes.name: loadedAll

nodes.name: getBytePos

nodes.name: setCharacterStream
nodes.summary: Returns a Writer that encodes characters as UTF-8 onto the large object's output stream at the resolved byte position.

nodes.name: truncate

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what SIARD Suite does: it archives relational databases into the standardized, software-independent SIARD 2.2 format so their contents stay readable long after the original DBMS is gone. The suite ships three faces over one core: a JavaFX desktop app, command-line tools, and per-database JDBC wrappers. The arc42-style architecture document in docs/sad adds the formal quality goals and the Swiss Federal Archives deployment constraints behind these design choices.

tour.title: The SIARD 2.2 Format
tour.description: Before touching any code, understand the artifact everything revolves around: a .siard file is a ZIP containing a metadata.xml plus one XML file per table. The metadata.xsd schema defines the siardArchive root covering database identity, schemas, tables, users and privileges, while table.xsd defines the row-level record structure. The copy under src/main/resources is what siard-api uses at runtime to validate archives it reads and writes.
tour.languageLesson: XSD schemas use lax wildcard validation (xsd:any processContents="lax") so a generic table.xsd can validate record elements whose concrete shape is only fixed by a per-table generated schema — a common pattern for extensible archival formats.

tour.title: Gradle Monorepo Layout
tour.description: settings.gradle.kts registers all twelve modules — siard-api, siard-cmd, siard-suite-app, the jdbc-* wrappers, sql-parser, zip64-file and siard-utilities — while the root build.gradle.kts enforces Java 21 and shared release plugins. Dependency versions are pinned centrally in the libs.versions.toml catalog, and mise.toml pins the Azul Zulu JavaFX JDK so every developer builds with the same toolchain. This map tells you which module owns each part of the pipeline you are about to see.
tour.languageLesson: Gradle Kotlin DSL (build.gradle.kts) gives type-safe build scripts: the version catalog in libs.versions.toml is consumed as typed accessors (libs.slf4j.api), so dependency coordinates are declared once and shared across modules.

tour.title: Core Archive API
tour.description: siard-api is the heart of the suite, and Archive.java is its front door — one of the most depended-upon files in the whole graph — defining the open/create/close lifecycle of a SIARD archive and access to its metadata. MetaData is the root metadata contract (database name, archiver, schemas, users, roles, privileges), Table gives access to records, and Value provides typed access to every cell across the full SQL type spectrum from primitives to LOBs, arrays and UDTs. Everything else in the project either produces or consumes through these interfaces.

tour.title: JAXB-Bound Implementation
tour.description: ArchiveImpl implements the Archive contract from Step 4 by treating the .siard file as a ZIP: it opens or creates the container, registers schemas and streams metadata.xml in and out. MetaDataImpl binds the siardArchive root element via JAXB — the module's build script wires XJC code generation from the very XSDs you saw in Step 2 straight into compileJava. Because the suite must still read older archives, Siard21ToSiard22Transformer upgrades SIARD 2.1 archives to 2.2 using a visitor that dispatches one method per metadata element type.
tour.languageLesson: JAXB maps XML schema types to generated Java classes via XJC, letting code manipulate XML through plain objects. The Visitor pattern used by the transformer adds an operation (here, version upgrade) over a fixed type hierarchy without modifying the visited classes.

tour.title: JDBC Abstraction Layer
tour.description: To talk to six different database families uniformly, jdbc-base wraps the standard java.sql interfaces: BaseDriver intercepts SIARD-specific URL schemes and delegates to the vendor driver, while BaseConnection, BaseDatabaseMetaData (~180 delegated methods) and BaseResultSet forward every call to the wrapped driver object. This delegation layer shields the rest of the suite from driver quirks so that each database module only has to override the behavior that actually differs. It is the seam between 'generic JDBC' and 'database-specific dialect'.
tour.languageLesson: These classes apply the Decorator (wrapper) pattern: each Base* class implements the same java.sql interface it wraps, so callers cannot tell whether they hold a raw driver object or the SIARD-aware wrapper.

tour.title: Concrete Driver: PostgreSQL
tour.description: jdbc-postgres shows the pattern from Step 6 instantiated for one database. PostgresDriver extends BaseDriver to build jdbc:postgresql: URLs and return PostgresConnection instances, which in turn create Postgres-flavored statements, LOB objects and structs. PostgresDatabaseMetaData goes beyond delegation by querying pg_catalog directly to surface Postgres UDTs, and PostgresResultSet translates native representations like bit strings, UUIDs and intervals into standard JDBC values. The sibling jdbc-mysql, jdbc-oracle, jdbc-mssql, jdbc-db2 and jdbc-access modules follow the same recipe.

tour.title: CLI: Downloading to SIARD
tour.description: SiardFromDb is the command-line entry point that turns a live database into a .siard archive. It resolves the right wrapper driver through SiardConnection, a singleton that maps JDBC subschemes to SIARD driver classes with overrides from jdbcdrivers.properties — the same registry users can edit to plug in new drivers. MetaDataFromDb then walks the database's schemas, tables, keys, routines and privileges into the archive metadata from Step 4, and PrimaryDataFromDb streams every table's rows into per-table XML files.

tour.title: CLI: Uploading Back to a DB
tour.description: SiardToDb runs the pipeline in reverse, uploading a SIARD archive's metadata and primary data into a target database — the restore half of the story. MetaDataToDb recreates schemas, tables, columns and UDTs (or drops existing ones), and PrimaryDataToDb streams records back over JDBC while handling LOB streaming and constraint ordering. ArchiveMapping and its siblings enable an important extra: restoring an archive into differently-named schemas by resolving archive names to their mapped target names.

tour.title: Desktop App Shell
tour.description: The JavaFX application starts at SiardApplication, which sets the MaterialFX theme, loads version properties and launches the root stage. Instead of dependency injection, the app uses a service-locator: ServicesFacade hands UI components the Navigator, Dialogs and ErrorHandler, while View.java acts as a central registry binding each FXML view/presenter pair to a navigation target. Navigator then moves between screens by loading those targets — a deliberately simple framework tailored to a wizard-style desktop tool.
tour.languageLesson: JavaFX pairs FXML (declarative UI markup) with a controller class loaded via FXMLLoader; LoadedView wraps that node-plus-controller pair so navigation can swap screens without each presenter knowing FXML loading details.

tour.title: Archive & Upload Wizards
tour.description: Building on the navigation shell, ArchiveStepperPresenter assembles the archive wizard as a step chain — choose DBMS, enter connection, edit metadata, download — inside a MaterialFX stepper control. ArchiveDownloadPresenter drives the final step by running the same download work you saw in SiardFromDb, but asynchronously through DbInteractionService with per-step progress rows. UploadStepperPresenter mirrors the flow for restoring a SIARD archive into a database, showing how the GUI is a thin orchestration layer over the siard-cmd and siard-api machinery.

tour.title: Browsing Archived Data
tour.description: Once an archive exists, GenericArchiveBrowserPresenter renders it as a tree of schemas, tables and metadata, dispatching each selected node to the right form and coordinating search dialogs and save/drop changes. RowsOverviewForm displays the actual row data as a lazily-loading table with cell previews — it consumes TableRecordDispenser, the pull-model API from siard-api that streams records with byte-position tracking so huge tables never load fully into memory. This step closes the loop: the same Archive/Table/Value interfaces from Step 4 that wrote the data now serve its interactive inspection.

tour.title: Testing & Release Pipeline
tour.description: Because the suite's promise is fidelity across six database engines, integration-tests.yml runs siard-cmd against a matrix of eight real database targets on every push and PR. The allDBs compose stack spins up PostgreSQL, Oracle XE, MSSQL, MySQL and DB2 containers locally, and docker/docker-compose.yaml provides the same live databases for JDBC-level tests. The release-guide document finishes the story with the manual smoke tests run against packaged distributions — including plain java -jar on the restricted SFA workstations mentioned back in the architecture doc.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrix builds run one job definition across many configurations in parallel — here each matrix axis entry is a database service, so the same upload/download test suite executes against every supported engine.
